intent: To illustrate public opinion poll results regarding the preferred direction of house prices in Britain.

requirements.question: Must the video explicitly state the 7% Rise figure, or is a clearly shortest Rise bar sufficient?
Must the video identify Fall as the most chosen answer at 42%, even though the provided narration only cites Rise?
Must the video show all four categories in rank order, or can it omit the middle categories?

units.claim: The Rise option is the least chosen answer, with only 7% saying rising prices would be good for Britain.

basis.note: Table value for Rise; the minimum among the four options.

accept: Only 7% say rising house prices would be good for Britain
Rise is the smallest group at 7%
units.evidence: The Rise bar must be visible with its 7% value label and must read as the shortest/lowest option.

units.claim: Fall is the most common answer, at 42%.

basis.note: Table value for Fall; the maximum among the four options.

accept: The largest group, 42%, says prices should fall
Fall is the top answer with 42%
units.evidence: The Fall bar must be visible, labelled 42%, and must read as the tallest/highest option.

units.claim: The full rank order from most to least chosen is Fall (42%), Stay (29%), Unsure (22%), Rise (7%).
accept: Order from most to least: Fall, Stay, Unsure, Rise
The ranking is Fall (42%), Stay (29%), Unsure (22%), Rise (7%)
Fall first, then Stay, then Unsure, then Rise
units.evidence: All four category bars/labels must be visible in a way that lets the viewer infer the descending order Fall, Stay, Unsure, Rise.

optional_valid: A separate Stay callout at 29% as the second-most common answer.
A separate Unsure callout at 22% as the third-most common answer.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded
